headline: GRAINS GIVE BACK THE CHINA POP AHEAD OF XI SUMMIT
lead: Corn settled $5.29, down 3½ cents, wheat down a penny and three-quarters, both giving back Monday's China-hope pop before Thursday's Trump-Xi summit even opens. Cattle fell 0.8% to $219.35 the day after a 2.4% jump on record-low placements, that's real profit-taking, not a reversal of the placements story.
teaser: Grains give back the China pop, cattle cool off, oil eyes a sixth straight losing day into the Xi summit.

one_number.unit: consecutive daily declines in crude oil
one_number.context: Oil's on pace for its longest losing streak since August 2025 as US-Iran talks revive, a supply story working against corn and diesel input costs at once.

yesterdays_call.note: Cattle closed $219.35, down 0.8% and well shy of $222, Monday's placement-driven pop didn't hold into today.
yesterdays_call.call_line: Called cattle up toward $222.00 ($221.15 when the call was made). It closed at $219.35.

action: Corn: no action above $5.29, but a settle below $5.27 says the China pop is fully unwound, price the next 10%.

sections.title: Grains Fade The Summit Pop
sections.body:
- Corn closed **$5.29**, down 3½ cents, and wheat slipped a penny and three-quarters as AgWeb flagged grains removing war premium and taking profit ahead of Thursday.
- Feedstuffs called it a broad corrective pullback with traders marking time before Trump and Xi actually sit down.
sections.so_what: The market already priced the summit optimism Monday; today unwound it.

sections.title: Cattle Cool After Placement Pop
sections.body:
- Live cattle backed off to **$219.35**, down 0.8%, a day after gaining 2.4% on record-low August feedlot placements.
- AgWeb is asking whether the rally attracts fund buying; today's pullback says the funds aren't chasing it yet.
- Beef magazine flags Santa Teresa import numbers and drought as the next placement swing factors.
sections.so_what: The placement story is intact; today's pullback is just profit-taking, not a reversal.

outside_the_pit.title: Trump Backs Diesel Export Ban At Record Prices
outside_the_pit.body: A ban would keep more diesel at home right into harvest and fall fieldwork, worth watching against the Oct. 1 trucker strike threat.

watch_list.desc: Trump-Xi summit opens; any confirmed soybean purchase headline is the next bean catalyst.
Weekly export sales; corn under 1.0 MMT confirms today's fade, not just a summit pause.
WTI below $89 extends the losing streak to a seventh day; watch diesel input costs into harvest.

daily_quote.text: If a problem cannot be solved, enlarge it.

source_summary: AgWeb, Feedstuffs, Beef Magazine, Dairy Herd, OilPrice.com, The Fence Post, CME/CBOT locked settlement data
